pages.caption: Adam and Eve hide among the trees after eating the fruit God told them not to eat.
Adam and his wife live in Eden. God tells Adam not to eat from one tree.
A clever snake asks the woman about God's command.
The woman answers, and the snake tells her she will not die.
The woman eats the fruit and gives some to her husband, who eats too.
They know they have no clothes and sew fig leaves together to cover themselves.
They hide among the trees, and God calls to Adam, asking where he is.

kjv.text: And the LORD God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?

pages.caption: Adam says he hid because he was afraid, then admits he ate the fruit.

kjv.text: And he said, Who told thee that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?
kjv.quote: Who told thee that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?

pages.caption: The woman says the snake tricked her and she ate.
God speaks to the snake about its future and the woman and her children.
God tells the woman and Adam that life will bring pain, hard work, and death.

kjv.text: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
kjv.quote: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.

pages.caption: Adam names his wife Eve. God makes clothes from animal skins and dresses them.
Adam and Eve leave Eden. God places special guards and a flaming sword by the way to the tree of life.
